text_blocks.snippet: A price decrease in vitamin C supplements due to an excess supply sale will likely lead to an increase in the quantity demanded of those supplements. This is because, according to the law of demand, lower prices generally incentivize consumers to purchase more of a product. There won't be a shift in the overall demand curve, but rather a movement along the existing curve as consumers respond to the lower price.

list.title: Excess Supply:
list.snippet: The scenario describes an "excess supply" or surplus of vitamin C supplements, meaning there's more available than what consumers are currently buying at the current price.

list.title: Price Reduction:
list.snippet: To address the excess supply, the store is lowering the price, making the product more affordable.

list.title: Increased Quantity Demanded:
list.snippet: As the price of vitamin C drops, more consumers will be willing and able to purchase it, leading to an increase in the quantity demanded.

list.title: No Shift in Demand:
list.snippet: This increase in quantity demanded is a direct result of the price change and does not indicate a change in consumer preferences or other factors that would shift the overall demand curve.
